raw_response:
I'm 59 this year, and I've been farming these 13 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. Finished senior high back in the day — not many farmers my age had that chance — so I can read the extension pamphlets and understand what the county ag technicians tell me. But book learning only gets you so far. What really matters is what I've seen with my own eyes on these fields.

My household has seven people: my wife and me, my elderly father, my son and daughter-in-law, and their two children. My son and his wife work at a garment factory in Handan, so they're gone most weeks but come back for wheat harvest and Spring Festival. That means day-to-day, it's me and my wife doing the farming, with my father helping when he can. The off-farm income is crucial — about 3,500 yuan a month they send back — but it also means we have less family labor at critical times. When wheat harvest hits in early June, I need them back, or I'll have to hire more custom labor.

I've divided the land into two blocks. The eastern 8 mu is my wheat-maize double-cropping land — been doing that for 20 years. The western 5.1 mu is cotton. I've kept the cotton because it brings good cash when prices are right, and after 15 years growing it, I know the rhythms of the crop.

**Winter wheat** — already in the ground since October 8th, variety Jinmai 47, an improved semi-dwarf type. I applied base fertilizer last fall: about 8 kg N per mu as urea, plus DAP and some potassium chloride. Now it's early March, wheat is at greening. I'm looking at the tillers — decent, not spectacular. Last year this block gave me 475 kg/mu. I'm targeting 500 kg/mu this year, which is ambitious but the stand looks uniform. I'll topdress with urea at jointing — about 22 kg urea per mu, which gives roughly 10 kg N. That brings my total N to 18 kg/mu. I thought about going to 20 kg N like the extension sheet recommends for 550 kg/mu targets, but fertilizer prices jumped again this spring, and I've got cotton seed and fertilizer to buy too. Eighteen kilograms is my compromise — it's what I did two years ago and got 490 kg/mu. My neighbor Lao Wang is pushing 20 kg N this year, but he's only growing wheat-maize, no cotton to finance.

For wheat irrigation, I'm planning three times: one now at greening-return (early March), one at jointing (late March/early April), and one at grain filling if May stays dry. Pumping water costs about 45 yuan per mu per time now with the metered wells, so three irrigations is 135 yuan per mu — real money. But my other neighbor Zhang Laohan only did two last year and lost yield in the hot May. Three is my safe number. I'll watch the sky; if we get a good rain in late April, I might skip the jointing irrigation and save 45 yuan per mu.

**Summer maize** — goes in right after wheat harvest, probably June 10–12. The window is brutal — if rain comes during harvest, I might miss the optimal planting date. I'll hire the custom combine-harvester for wheat (about 300 yuan for the 8 mu), then immediately run the planter for maize. I don't own the planter, so that's another 30 yuan/mu. Variety will be Zhengdan 958 hybrid, about 40 yuan/mu for seed. I use fresh hybrid seed every year — saved seed loses vigor, and with only 8 mu I can't afford a bad stand.

Maize fertilizer: total 16 kg N per mu, split between base compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea at the big trumpet stage in mid-July. Two irrigations for maize — one at silking and one in August if needed. I'm expecting about 550 kg/mu if the summer rains are normal. Last year I got 520 kg/mu because July was too wet and I didn't irrigate, but I also didn't lose money on pumping.

**Cotton** — planting around April 22–25, when soil temperature hits 15°C consistently. I use Bt hybrid cotton, usually Jimian or a similar local certified variety, about 60 yuan/mu for seed. Cotton is labor-hungry but the returns per mu are better than maize when lint prices hold above 15 yuan per jin. Total N around 14 kg/mu in three splits: base before planting, first topdress at early flowering (early July), second at peak boll stage (August). I'll irrigate twice — once at flowering and once at boll stage. The real cost is picking labor. My wife and I will do the early picks in September, but for the main flush in October, I'll need to hire 8 days of picking labor at 120 yuan per day. Even with that expense, cotton net return usually beats maize on a per-mu basis, which is why I keep that 5.1 mu in cotton despite the headache.

Total cash I'm looking at spending this year is about 7,900 yuan. That's manageable because of my son's factory income, but without it I'd probably cut the wheat N rate back to 15 kg/mu and skip one maize irrigation. The biggest worry is the wheat-maize turnaround — if the custom harvester breaks down or my son can't get leave, I might have to plant maize late, and every day past June 15 costs me yield. I'm also watching the cotton market. If lint prices drop below 14 yuan per jin before harvest, I'll regret not putting that 5.1 mu into wheat-maize too. But that's the gamble of farming.
